choices.misconception: I found that the two products differ by 4 but subtracted them the wrong way round.
I thought moving 2 from one factor to the other leaves the product unchanged.
I remembered that 2025 × 2025 is 1 more than 2026 × 2024 and assumed the difference here is also 1.
I thought the product changes by the 2 that was moved from one factor to the other.

hints: Multiplying out two four-digit products is slow and easy to get wrong. Look for the short way: both numbers are 2025 plus or minus 2. Testing small numbers like 5 × 5 and 7 × 3 can show the pattern.

solutions.reliable: Split both products so they share 2025 × 2023. First, 2025 × 2025 = 2025 × 2023 + 2025 × 2. Second, 2027 × 2023 = 2025 × 2023 + 2 × 2023. The shared part cancels, leaving 2 × 2025 - 2 × 2023 = 2 × 2 = 4. The transferable idea: when numbers are suspiciously close together, a minute spent looking for the trick saves several minutes of error-prone grinding.
solutions.elegant: Small cases: 5 × 5 - 7 × 3 = 25 - 21 = 4 and 10 × 10 - 12 × 8 = 100 - 96 = 4. Moving 2 from one side of a square to the other loses a 2 by 2 corner, so the difference is always 4.

whyOnTest: Suspiciously convenient numbers signal a short way in; the skill is deciding to look for it instead of multiplying out.
